To study a specific topic for an interview effectively, ==break down the core concepts from the job description and build adaptable stories or explanations around them rather than trying to memorize everything==. [[1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=03WZ8O77O_E&t=601), [2](https://consultadd.com/blog/last-minute-interview-tips-a-60-minute-prep-plan)]

Step 1: Analyze the Requirements

- **Highlight keywords:** Read the job description to find the exact technical skills, tools, or concepts the employer wants.

- **Define your depth:** Decide if you need a high-level overview (like a project manager knowing budgeting tools) or deep technical mastery (like an engineer knowing specific code functions). [[1](https://www.coursera.org/in/articles/how-to-prepare-for-an-interview), [2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=03WZ8O77O_E&t=601)]

Step 2: Build Core Explanations

- **Draft 90-second summaries:** Write short, clear explanations for the major sub-topics.

- **Focus on trade-offs:** For complex subjects, learn the pros, cons, and alternative choices so you can discuss decisions critically. [[1](https://www.quora.com/Whats-the-best-strategy-to-study-for-a-job-interview-with-a-lot-of-technical-material-to-memorize), [2](https://consultadd.com/blog/last-minute-interview-tips-a-60-minute-prep-plan)]

Step 3: Use the STAR Method for Practical Application

- **Recall real experiences:** Connect the study topic to real projects you worked on.

- **Structure with STAR:** Frame your answers using **Situation** (context), **Task** (your goal), **Action** (what you did), and **Result** (the measurable outcome).

- **Reuse stories:** One strong project story can answer multiple different questions about problem-solving, failure, or leadership. [[1](https://capd.mit.edu/resources/the-star-method-for-behavioral-interviews/), [2](https://www.quora.com/Whats-the-best-strategy-to-study-for-a-job-interview-with-a-lot-of-technical-material-to-memorize), [3](https://consultadd.com/blog/last-minute-interview-tips-a-60-minute-prep-plan)]

Step 4: Practice Out Loud

- **Avoid scripting:** Paraphrase your notes and speak them out loud instead of memorizing word-for-word text.

- **Simulate pressure:** Practice explaining the topic as if you are teaching it to a coworker or recording yourself on video. [[1](https://consultadd.com/blog/last-minute-interview-tips-a-60-minute-prep-plan)]
